title: Dual-stream architecture with asymmetric clinical safety evaluation for colorectal histopathology — reproducibility code
description:
Companion code for Nasser-eddine et al., “Dual-stream architecture with asymmetric clinical safety evaluation for colorectal histopathology” (unpublished manuscript).

This record archives the tagged GitHub repository: a single self-contained Jupyter notebook (reproduce.ipynb) that defines the dual-stream classifier head, the Gated Attention MIL aggregator, the Asymmetric Clinical Safety Score (ACSS) and the cross-validation inline, and reproduces every headline result of the paper — patch level (F4/S4/F6: accuracy 92.37%/93.39%/92.67%, ACSS 95.92/95.88/95.56) and slide level (91-slide cohort: 88.4 ± 2.7%, zero CAR→NOR for F4) — from pre-computed de-identified embeddings. Dependencies: torch, numpy, scikit-learn.

v1.1 corrects the slide-level protocol. In v1.0 the held-out fold was used both to stop training and to report the result (F4: 92.8 ± 1.1%); from v1.1, early stopping is decided on a stratified 20% of each training block and the held-out fold is evaluated once, at the end. The patch-level results do not change.

The de-identified data artifacts this code consumes (the shared test_embeddings.npz, the per-model classifier heads <M>_head.pth, and the 91-slide caches external_cache_<M>.pt) are deposited in the companion data record, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21327829. Raw whole-slide images and patch-level image arrays are NOT included in either record: they contain patient material and are available on reasonable request to the corresponding author, subject to HUC approval and a data-processing agreement.
